implementation: Native stdio language-server lifecycle with framed JSON-RPC via existing LLVM JSON support
Full-document synchronization, monotonically increasing versions and owned source overlays
Recheck open roots and optional explicit project entry against current unsaved imports/packages
Publish original UTF-16 diagnostic ranges, codes, severity, source and open-buffer versions
Deduplicate graph diagnostics and clear obsolete/closed URI publications
Bound headers, frame bodies, JSON nesting, open buffers and compiler graphs

qualification.protocol_harness: Independent Python stdlib subprocess/pipe client; no Python dependency in server
coverage: Initialization, shutdown/exit, request errors and parse-error recovery
UTF-16 supplementary scalar ranges and Unicode/escaped/local file URIs
Full edits, sequential full replacements, rejected ranged edits and older versions
Changed imported signatures and duplicate diagnostic suppression
Closing dependencies reverts to disk; unopened dependency errors clear after edits
Explicit project packages and shared placement mode without hardware access
Unsaved file/disk isolation, normalized aliases and localhost URI clearing
Oversized document/frame/header rejection, JSON depth, truncated/duplicate headers and wrong charset
Large numeric IDs/versions are bounded before conversion
qualification.third_party_sanitization: LLVM is not rebuilt with sanitizers

limitations: Full-document sync only; no incremental changes, hover, navigation, completion or formatting
Synchronous checks; no debounce, background cancellation, queued-edit coalescing or asynchronous stale-result suppression
No real editor or additional OS qualification
Explicit startup manifest only; no discovery, live configuration changes or package installation
No filesystem watcher or atomic disk snapshot
Source-less diagnostics are logged without invented ranges
